sources.name: GLA Digital Connectivity Infrastructure Guidance
sources.fact: Adopted November 2024 guidance implements London Plan SI6 for digital connectivity infrastructure in new and existing development

sources.name: Ofcom Connected Nations Spring 2026
sources.fact: January 2026 snapshot reports UK full-fibre/gigabit availability and mobile coverage; national availability is not parcel service proof

sources.name: Ofcom planned network deployments 2026
sources.fact: Operator plans project increased full-fibre/gigabit coverage to 2028/29; plans are forward-looking and not guaranteed build at a parcel

sources.name: Ofcom coverage and speeds
sources.fact: Ofcom publishes current and planned network coverage data and coverage checkers

sources.name: Ofcom infrastructure research
sources.fact: Connected Nations infrastructure reports distinguish current coverage from planned deployment

sources.name: NPPF communications infrastructure
sources.fact: Planning policy supports expansion of full fibre and mobile networks and requires relevant evidence for telecoms development

sources.name: Local planning authority telecoms guidance
sources.fact: Local plans can support fixed/mobile rollout; planning support does not establish an operator service order

sources.name: New build connectivity developer guidance
sources.fact: Building Regulations require new homes to install the fastest connection available within the statutory framework and future-proof physical infrastructure

sources.name: Project Gigabit May 2026 OMR
sources.fact: BDUK market review maps existing/planned gigabit infrastructure over three years; planned coverage is not completed service

sources.name: Telecommunications Modernisation
sources.fact: 2026 programme covers copper-to-fibre and mobile network modernisation; national transition is not parcel availability proof

sources.name: Telecoms Statement of Strategic Priorities 2026
sources.fact: Designated April 2026 priorities include fixed/wireless infrastructure, consumer interests, spectrum and resilience

sources.name: London Infrastructure Framework 2026
sources.fact: Digital connectivity including data centres is one of London’s growth-critical infrastructure sectors

examples: UK or London coverage percentage does not prove a candidate parcel has a serviceable connection
Operator planned deployment is not completed fibre at the property boundary
Building Regulations new-build duty does not prove an existing parcel currently has gigabit service
Mobile outdoor coverage does not equal indoor or site-specific service quality
Planning support for telecoms does not replace operator survey/wayleave evidence
Project Gigabit planned area status is not a guaranteed completion date
Copper-to-fibre modernisation is a transition context, not parcel-specific resilience proof
No digital-connectivity uplift is assigned without address/site-level current service evidence
